rules.title: Native APIs before libraries
rules.what: Use platform APIs before adding a dependency: fetch, Intl, URL, structuredClone, Array methods cover most needs that once required lodash/moment.
rules.why: Each library adds bundle weight and supply-chain surface for work the platform does natively - parsed and shipped to every user on every visit.
rules.how: Check MDN for the native API first; if importing, prefer modular imports of the single function; verify tree-shaking in the bundle.

patterns.note: Heavy library import; check for a native API or lighter module.
moment: prefer date-fns, dayjs or Intl.*; moment is in maintenance mode.

verify.how: Bundle analysis: library weight and used-export count recorded.

limits: Existing heavy usage may make a staged migration cheaper than a rewrite; measure.

rules.title: No sync I/O on the request path
rules.what: In Node servers/handlers: no readFileSync/writeFileSync/execSync/pbkdf2Sync; async I/O and worker threads for CPU-bound work.
rules.why: The Node event loop serves all requests with one thread per core: a single sync call parks every concurrent request behind it.
rules.how: fs/promises, async crypto (scrypt async), worker_threads or a job queue for heavy computation.

patterns.note: Sync I/O call; verify it is startup/CLI-only, not on the request path.

verify.how: Load test: one slow request does not raise p95 of concurrent unrelated requests.

limits: Startup-only reads (config, templates) are deliberate; a comment marks them.

rules.title: No unbounded Promise.all over collections
rules.what: Do not Promise.all over an unbounded collection; use a concurrency-limited runner (p-limit pattern, batching) sized to the downstream capacity.
rules.why: Promise.all fires every request at once: the downstream service sees a spike identical to a DoS, and the failure mode is a timeout storm, not a queue.
rules.how: Limit concurrency to what the downstream and the event loop handle; batch by page; retry per item with caps.

patterns.note: Promise.all over a mapped collection; candidate - verify the collection is bounded or a limiter is used.

verify.how: Large collection: concurrent in-flight requests stay within the stated limit.

limits: Small, known-size collections are fine; the rule targets data that grows.

rules.title: Await in loops only with cause
rules.what: An await inside a for/forEach over data is either justified (real dependency between iterations) or replaced (batch, Promise.all-limited, single query).
rules.why: Sequential awaits pay full latency per item where the work is independent; the total time is the sum where it could be the max or one call.
rules.how: Identify the dependency; if none, batch the call or run bounded-parallel; if there is one, comment it.

patterns.note: await in a for-of loop; candidate for batching/parallelism.

verify.how: Calls-per-task count and total latency measured against the budget.

limits: Rate-limited or order-dependent work must stay sequential; that is the documented cause.

rules.title: Tree-shake and measure the bundle
rules.what: The build produces per-route chunks, imports are named (not namespace), and bundle size is tracked in CI with a budget.
rules.why: An unmeasured bundle grows every sprint; a tracked budget catches the regression at the PR that caused it, which is the only cheap moment to fix it.
rules.how: Rollup/webpack/esbuild analysis output tracked in CI; named imports; dynamic import for heavy optional features.

verify.how: CI bundle report exists with a size budget that fails the build when crossed.

rules.title: JSON without silent serialization traps
rules.what: Parse and serialise JSON deliberately: no parsing inside hot loops of identical payloads, no JSON.stringify in high-frequency logs, no silent lossy struct conversions.
rules.why: JSON parse/stringify of large objects in hot paths is CPU paid per event; and silent loss (undefined, Date to string) creates re-work downstream.
rules.how: Parse once and reuse, cap logged payload size, use structured loggers with lazy serialisation.

patterns.note: JSON (de)serialisation of request payloads; candidate if in a hot path or log.

verify.how: CPU profile of the hot path shows serialisation within the stated share.

rules.title: Maps and Sets for lookups in loops
rules.what: Index data in a Map or Set before a loop instead of calling includes/indexOf/find on a growing array inside it.
rules.why: Each linear search walks the array; nested in a loop the work becomes quadratic and collapses on real volumes.
rules.how: const byId = new Map(items.map(i => [i.id, i])); then byId.get(id).

patterns.note: Linear search inside a loop; candidate if the searched array grows.

verify.how: No linear search over a growing array inside a loop.

rules.title: Reuse clients, abort what is no longer needed
rules.what: Create HTTP and database clients once and share them; give fetches a deadline with AbortController and cancel them when the result is no longer wanted.
rules.why: A client per call loses connection reuse; a fetch nobody waits for any more still costs the network, the server and the battery.
rules.how: One axios instance or keep-alive agent per service; AbortSignal.timeout(ms); abort on unmount or on a newer request.

patterns.note: Client construction; fine once per module, a defect inside a function called per request.

verify.how: Navigation/unmount test asserts in-flight requests are aborted; client created once.

rules.title: Pause polling when nobody looks
rules.what: Replace setInterval polling with events (WebSocket, SSE, push) where possible; otherwise pause it when the page is hidden and widen the interval.
rules.why: A polling timer keeps querying the server and waking the radio for a tab nobody is looking at.
rules.how: document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', ...) to pause; Server-Sent Events for server updates; clearInterval on teardown.

patterns.note: Interval timer in a file that never checks page visibility.

verify.how: Polling is paused on hidden pages, or replaced by an event source.

rules.title: No implicit globals
rules.what: Scope variables to modules or functions; never assign undeclared variables or declare top-level vars in classic scripts.
rules.why: A global stays alive for the whole page lifetime and is visible to every script: memory held longer than needed and collisions between scripts.
rules.how: type="module" scripts or an IIFE; const/let inside functions; 'use strict' turns implicit globals into errors; assign required globals explicitly as properties.
